behaviors.name: network_communication
behaviors.why: Initiating outbound network connections can be used to contact command-and-control servers or exfiltrate data.

behaviors.name: network_data_reception
behaviors.why: Receiving data over the network may indicate downloading payloads or receiving commands from an attacker.

behaviors.name: dns_activity
behaviors.why: DNS queries can be used for covert communication or domain generation algorithms in malware.

behaviors.name: data_exfil_http
behaviors.why: Sending data via HTTP(S) is a common method for exfiltrating sensitive information to external servers.

behaviors.name: data_exfil_socket
behaviors.why: Raw socket communication can be used to send stolen data directly to an attacker-controlled server.

behaviors.name: data_exfil_scp
behaviors.why: Using SCP to transfer files may indicate exfiltration of data to remote systems.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: n.startswith(('paramiko.SSHClient.', 'scp.SCPClient.', 'os.system')) and 'scp' in n

behaviors.name: data_exfil_webhook
behaviors.why: Webhooks can be abused to send data to external services without direct interaction.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: n.startswith(('requests.post', 'urllib.request.urlopen')) and 'webhook' in n.lower()

behaviors.name: data_collection_stdin
behaviors.why: Reading from standard input may capture user-typed sensitive data or credentials.

behaviors.name: lateral_movement_ssh
behaviors.why: SSH connections to other hosts may indicate attempts to move laterally within a network.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: n.startswith(('paramiko.SSHClient.connect', 'os.system', 'subprocess.run')) and ('ssh' in n or 'ssh' in n.lower())

behaviors.name: self_propagation_scp
behaviors.why: Copying files via SCP to other systems could be a sign of self-replicating malware.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: n.startswith(('paramiko.SSHClient.', 'scp.SCPClient.', 'os.system')) and 'scp' in n

behaviors.name: fs_read
behaviors.why: Reading files from the filesystem may involve accessing sensitive data like credentials or documents.

behaviors.name: fs_write
behaviors.why: Writing files can be used to drop payloads, store stolen data, or modify system configurations.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: n in ('open', 'pathlib.Path.write_text', 'pathlib.Path.write_bytes', 'os.open', 'io.open') and any(m in n for m in ['write', 'w+', 'a+'])

behaviors.name: payload_dumping
behaviors.why: Writing large binary or encoded data to disk may indicate dumping of embedded payloads or memory dumps.

behaviors.name: fs_enum
behaviors.why: Enumerating files or directories helps attackers discover valuable data or system layout.

behaviors.name: credential_access_bruteforce
behaviors.why: Attempting multiple authentication combinations suggests brute-force attacks on credentials.

behaviors.name: credential_access
behaviors.why: Accessing credential stores or configuration files can lead to privilege escalation or data theft.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: any(kw in n for kw in ['keyring', 'getpass', '.aws', '.ssh', 'credentials', 'password', 'secret'])

behaviors.name: command_execution
behaviors.why: Executing system commands can lead to full system compromise or lateral movement.

behaviors.name: dynamic_code_exec
behaviors.why: Executing code dynamically (e.g., from strings) can hide malicious logic and evade detection.

behaviors.name: dynamic_code_load
behaviors.why: Loading code from external sources at runtime can introduce untrusted or malicious functionality.

behaviors.name: reflection_abuse
behaviors.why: Using reflection to access or modify internal program state can bypass security controls.

behaviors.name: crypto_activity
behaviors.why: Cryptographic operations may be used to encrypt data for ransomware or decrypt payloads.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: n.startswith(('cryptography.', 'Crypto.', 'pycryptodome.', 'hashlib.', 'hmac.')) or 'encrypt' in n or 'decrypt' in n

behaviors.name: deobfuscation
behaviors.why: Decoding or decompressing data may reveal hidden malicious code or configuration.

behaviors.name: obfuscation_dynamic_config
behaviors.why: Dynamically generating or modifying configuration can hide malicious behavior or C2 addresses.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: any(kw in n for kw in ['config', 'json.loads', 'yaml.load', 'ast.literal_eval']) and ('exec' in n or 'eval' in n or 'compile' in n)

behaviors.name: system_recon
behaviors.why: Gathering system information helps attackers understand the environment for further exploitation.

behaviors.name: process_recon
behaviors.why: Enumerating running processes can identify security tools or valuable targets.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: n.startswith(('psutil.process_iter', 'psutil.pids', 'os.popen', 'subprocess.check_output')) and ('ps' in n or 'tasklist' in n or 'proc' in n)

behaviors.name: permission_manipulation
behaviors.why: Changing file or process permissions can escalate privileges or maintain access.

behaviors.name: defense_evasion_daemon
behaviors.why: Running as a background daemon or service can help malware persist undetected.

behaviors.name: defense_evasion
behaviors.why: Techniques that disable or avoid security tools increase the likelihood of successful attacks.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: any(kw in n for kw in ['disable', 'bypass', 'kill', 'terminate', 'remove', 'delete', 'uninstall']) and ('av' in n or 'antivirus' in n or 'defender' in n or 'security' in n)

behaviors.name: defense_evasion_gui
behaviors.why: Hiding windows or GUI elements can prevent user awareness of malicious activity.

behaviors.name: persistence_registry
behaviors.why: Modifying Windows registry keys ensures malware runs after reboot.

behaviors.name: persistence_cron
behaviors.why: Adding cron jobs or scheduled tasks enables persistent execution on Unix-like systems.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: n.startswith(('crontab', 'subprocess.run', 'os.system')) and ('cron' in n or 'at ' in n or 'scheduled' in n)

behaviors.name: keylogging
behaviors.why: Capturing keystrokes can steal passwords, messages, and other sensitive input.

behaviors.name: user_input_prompt
behaviors.why: Prompting for user input can be used to phish credentials or trick users into enabling malicious actions.

behaviors.name: clipboard_abuse
behaviors.why: Reading or modifying the clipboard can steal sensitive data or inject malicious content.

behaviors.name: screenshot
behaviors.why: Taking screenshots can capture sensitive information displayed on the screen.

behaviors.name: gui_abuse
behaviors.why: Manipulating GUI elements can simulate user actions or hide malicious windows.

behaviors.name: install_hook
behaviors.why: Installing hooks into system or application events can intercept sensitive data or control flow.
